findings.title: KeyError when Integration metadata has no 'sender'
findings.body: In GitHubInstallation.dispatch, the new verification step does `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]`. The `sender` key is optional: `build_integration` only adds it `if state.get("sender")`, so Integration rows created through the pipeline itself (the `Integration.DoesNotExist` branch, e.g. when the installation webhook hasn't been processed yet) never get `sender` in metadata, and older rows may lack it too. If such an integration later has no OrganizationIntegration (e.g. the org integration was deleted and the user re-runs setup, or the first org-linking happens after a pipeline-created row exists), this line raises KeyError and the user gets a 500 instead of either succeeding or seeing the new failure page. Use `integration.metadata.get("sender")` and explicitly decide whether a missing sender should fail closed or be skipped.

findings.title: Authenticated-user check is skipped when the Integration row doesn't exist yet
findings.body: The PR's goal is to block linking a GitHub App installation when the OAuth-authenticated GitHub user differs from the user who installed the app. However, in GitHubInstallation.dispatch the check only runs when an Integration row already exists (the webhook-created path). In the `except Integration.DoesNotExist: return pipeline.next_step()` branch, the pipeline proceeds to `build_integration`, which calls `get_installation_info(state["installation_id"])` — an app-JWT call that returns data for *any* installation of the app — with no comparison against `github_authenticated_user` at all. An attacker who learns or guesses a victim's installation_id (these are sequential integers) can still attach that installation to their own Sentry org whenever the victim's Integration row is absent (webhook delivery failed or delayed, or installation predates webhook handling), which is the same hijack this PR intends to prevent. Consider validating the authenticated user in this branch too, or refusing to proceed until the installation webhook has created the Integration row.

findings.title: Unhandled exceptions from GitHub HTTP calls in OAuthLoginView produce 500s
findings.body: OAuthLoginView.dispatch calls `safe_urlopen(...)` (line 423) outside any try/except, and `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` (line 434) is also unguarded — it performs an HTTP GET to api.github.com and calls `.json()` on the response. Network failures, timeouts, or a non-JSON error body from GitHub will raise and surface as a 500 during installation, even though the stated intent of this change is that all OAuth/token failures show the 'We could not verify the authenticity of the installation request' page. Only the body-parsing step is wrapped (and with a bare `except Exception`). Wrap the token exchange and user-info calls and render the error page on failure.

findings.title: No positive test for the sender-match branch; missing-sender crash untested
findings.body: The new test `test_github_user_mismatch` only covers the failure case. There is no test for the success path of the new check: Integration row exists (created by the installation webhook) with no OrganizationIntegration, and the OAuth-authenticated user matches `metadata["sender"]["login"]` — which is the primary real-world flow for users who install the app directly from github.com. If the comparison were inverted or `github_authenticated_user` state binding broke, the suite would still pass. There is also no test for an Integration whose metadata lacks `sender`, which currently raises KeyError (500) instead of a handled outcome.
